text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Most newspapers lead with appointment of Saleh Sulong as chairman of DRB-Hicom group, replacing the late Yahaya Ahmad, who was killed in a helicopter crash on Monday. Saleh was deputy chairman of the group.

-- Air crash investigators are mystified over the discovery that one of the two blades belonging to Agusta 109P helicopter that ferried the late Yahaya had split into two, something which is considered almost impossible by the aircraft manufacturer Agusta Corp.
-- Malaysia's king said South Africa had all the ingredients of an African tiger economy and the Malaysian private sector found the country to be one of the most attractive investment destinations.

-- The Malaysian government has received a new proposal for the rescue of bankrupt aircraft maker NV Fokker, after the original proposal from Dutch investors was rejected by Khazanah Holdings Bhd last month.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said the government will always hold in high esteem the contributions made to the nation by the late Yahaya Ahmad.

-- Rashid Hussain Bhd, the financial service group, looks forward to tapping new business opportunities following the entry of property group Malaysian Resources Corp Bhd as a substantial shareholder in the group.
-- Malaysia will keep to its commitment of liberalising its domestic fund management industry, but at a pace that it is comfortable with, Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim says.
-- The government is drafting amendments to the Medical Act 1971 to allow for the practice of traditional medicine in hospitals.
-- The Employees Provident Fund, with more than 112 billion ringgit in assets, is in the final stage of drawing up a programme to invest overseas, Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said.
